'''R3-T7''' was a [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3-series astromech droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nubia/Legends|Nubia]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] served the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] on a [[Patrol ship/Legends|patrol ship]] before moving into the service of an up-and-coming [[Unidentified senator (R3-T7)|senator]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. 

After the senator was sent to his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] on charges of corruption, the droid was bought by a [[Unidentified merchant (R3-T7)|merchant]] in Coruscant's [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]]. R3-T7 was eventually attacked, causing frequent memory wipes when it shorted out. The wipes caused it wander around aimlessly until its master collected it. After the droid was abandoned by the merchant, R3-T7 had an unknown fate.

==Biography==
===A cutting edge droid===
The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] R3-T7 was manufactured at the [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] plant in [[Rordis City]] on the<ref name="FF123" /> [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nubia/Legends|Nubia]], during a time when the [[R3-series astromech droid/Legends|R3 series]] of [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] were at the cutting edge of technology. In the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="FF123" /> a conflict that started in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|II}} to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> R3-T7 served aboard a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Patrol ship/Legends|patrol ship]]. Though details of this part of the droid's life were sketchy, it was assumed R3-T7 travelled through many parts of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] while serving.<ref name="FF123" />

[[File:Industrial_Automaton.svg|thumb|right|300px|R3-T7 was manufactured by Industrial Automaton (logo pictured).]]
At some point, R3-T7 fell into the hands of an up-and-coming [[Unidentified senator (R3-T7)|senator]] taking residence on<ref name="FF123" /> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="FF123" /> another planet in the Core Worlds.<ref name="TEA" /> It spent three years in the senator's service, doing tasks such as keeping tabs of its master's diary and taking care of his security. The droid's peaceful [[Standard day/Legends|days]] were interrupted when the senator was caught up in a political scandal during the time approaching the Clone Wars. He was brought before the [[Senate Disciplinary Committee]], found guilty of corruption, and sent to serve time in [[Prison/Legends|prison]] on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="FF123" />

===Errand runner attacked===
Within the course of a few [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], R3-T7 was left without a master and was auctioned off along with the senator's other possessions. No buyers were interested in [[Currency/Legends|paying]] the droid's reserve price, as few Coruscant people had need for a droid like R3-T7. It was finally bought, price reduced considerably, by a lowlife [[Unidentified merchant (R3-T7)|merchant]] operating from Coruscant's [[Uscru Entertainment District/Legends|Uscru Entertainment District]], as they needed an assistant to do errands, deliver goods, and receive payments.<ref name="FF123" />  

[[File:R3-T7Alleyway-AOTC.jpg|thumb|left|350px|R3-T7 rolled along a street on Coruscant.]]
As the droid descended into the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant Underworld]], R3-T7 found itself in all sorts of criminal activity. While on an errand for its new master, the droid was attacked by a street gang that blasted it at point-blank range. Though the attack should have been the end of R3-T7, its owner was determined to not throw away the droid just yet. It was fixed through a back-alley repair job, but the droid was not as it once was; R3-T7's blast damage was not fully repaired, and it frequently shorted out in flashes of electrical charges. This happened usually once a day, during which the droid's memories were wiped, causing it to wander aimlessly until the merchant collected it.<ref name="FF123" />

R3-T7's master eventually gave up on the droid and abandoned it on the street.<ref name="FF123" /> Just before the outbreak of the Clone Wars, the droid wandered the streets of Coruscant's [[CoCo Town/Legends|CoCo Town]].<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|71|R3-T7}}</ref> In 22 BBY,<ref name="NEC" /> the droid strolled along a street in the Uscru District with pedestrian traffic as the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] pulled [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]] out of<ref name="AOTC" /> the [[Nightclub/Legends|nightclub]] and [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] hall known as the [[Outlander Club/Legends|Outlander Club]].<ref name="CSWE2">{{CSWECite|II|431|Outlander Club}}</ref> What eventually became of R3-T7 was not known. It was likely the droid ended up in a garbage pit, though it was possible a droid appreciator came across R3-T7 and realized how advanced the droid was.<ref name="FF123" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:R3T7side-FF123.png|thumb|right|200px|A profile view of R3-T7]]
Standing at 0.96 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, the clear-domed R3-T7 had a shabby exterior of [[Color/Legends|white]], lime green, yellow plating and two scorch marks across its body. After the droid was shot by a street gang, dramatic blue flashes of electrical charges came from the droid<ref name="FF123" /> and engulfed its body.<ref name="Hasbro" />

R3-T7, with its military programming,<ref name="NewFF44">{{FactFile2014|44|R3 1-2|R3 astromech droids}}</ref> proudly served aboard the Galactic Republic starship and enjoyed the happy years when the senator was its master. The R3 series of droid were regarded as prestigious, reflecting well on ambitious politicians who owned them. The senator's ownership of R3-T7 showed an impressive knowledge of droids and showed a possible previous military career. R3-T7 frequently shorted out, wiping its memory and eventually making its new merchant master lose hope in the droid.<ref name="FF123" />

==Equipment==
Like other R3 units, R3-T7 had an upgraded [[Intellex V/Legends|Intellex V]] operating computer.<ref name="FF123" /> The droid brain allowed the droid to have the senator's tasks be well in its capability.<ref name="NewFF44" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|An interesting-looking but puzzling choice for a preview figure, this figure is hard to find in Episode II.|R3-T7's entry in ''Star Wars: The Ultimate Action Figure Collection''|<ref name="Action" />}}
R3-T7 was first pictured when the droid appeared in "[[Making Episode II Webdocs|A Twinkle Beyond Pluto]]," a documentary detailing the making of the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. The web documentary<ref name="ATBP">{{SW|url=video/a-twinkle-beyond-pluto|series=Making Episode II Webdocs|text=Part 5: A Twinkle Beyond Pluto}}</ref> released on [[July 31]], [[2001]].<ref name="ATBP Date">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/me2/archive.html|text=''Making Episode II Webdocs'' archive}}</ref> R3-T7 was identified when the toy company [[Hasbro]] produced an action figure of the character in [[2002]] as part of the [[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|Star Wars: Power of the Jedi toyline]] as a "sneak preview" for Episode II.<ref name="Hasbro" /> The droid then first appeared in ''Attack of the Clones'',<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> which released on [[May 16]], 2002.<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> The droid was originally meant to appear in the film's [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] scenes and was on the scene's set, outside the eatery, but the character was edited out by digital artists at [[Industrial Light & Magic]] when they added the scene's background exterior.<ref name="Insider69">{{InsiderCite|69|Star Wars Q&A|''Star Wars'' Q&A}}</ref> In the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Action Figure Collection]]'', author [[Stephen J. Sansweet]] reflected on the release of the action figure, stating it was a puzzling choice for a preview figure.<ref name="Action">''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Action Figure Collection]]''</ref>
